**Drafting compact decoder**

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module decoder_8bit
#(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    generate
        if (N == 8) begin : gen_decode8
            wire [15:0] low_miss;
            wire [15:0] high_miss;
            wire [255:0] decoded;

            for (genvar p = 0; p < 16; p = p + 1) begin : gen_predecode
                localparam [3:0] CODE = p;
                assign low_miss[p] = |(in[3:0] ^ CODE);
                assign high_miss[p] = |(in[7:4] ^ CODE);
            end

            for (genvar q = 0; q < 256; q = q + 1) begin : gen_outputs
                assign decoded[q] = ~(high_miss[q / 16] | low_miss[q % 16]);
            end

            always @(*) begin
                out = decoded;
            end
        end else begin : gen_other_width
            always @(*) begin
                out = {{(1<<N)-1{1'b0}}, 1'b1} << in;
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The variable one-hot shift can produce a deep or heavily loaded decode network. Maximum arrival is sensitive to both decode depth and the fanout of shared input terms.",
  "rewrite": "Use two parallel 4-to-16 active-low predecoders, followed by one two-input NOR function per output. Each predecode result feeds exactly 16 output functions. This exposes a shallow NAND4/NOR2-style implementation with shared input inversions.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to reduce maximum data arrival through a shallow, balanced decode structure. Actual improvement, buffer insertion, and slew/capacitance compliance require the specified mapping and STA flow; no numerical timing result is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The logical structure contains 32 four-bit predecode terms and 256 two-input output functions, plus input inversions and mapping-inserted buffers. Sharing should keep area economical, but compliance with the 2859.992960um2 cap has not been measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For N=8, output bit q is high exactly when both input nibbles match the corresponding nibbles of q, so out equals the original 256-bit one-hot shift for every binary input. The module interface, parameter declaration/default, output width and unsignedness are unchanged. Other parameter values retain the original expression. No state, assumptions, undefined outputs, or external dependencies are introduced."
}
